paragraphs.source_en: The reason Songs of Love was able to circulate so widely lies, on the one hand, in the lively vividness of its thought and content: it swept away the old habit by which every work of the literati had to contain religious matter, and thus had progressive significance; on the other hand, it also achieved something distinctive in art. In metrical structure, Songs of Love adopts the form of folk song: apart from a few pieces of six or eight lines, most poems have four lines, each line with six syllables, pausing every two syllables, that is, four lines, six syllables, and three pauses. Its rhythm is clear, it rolls readily off the tongue, and it can also be sung to folk melodies, giving it a strong folk-song flavor. Some pieces use the technique of plain sketching; they are natural and fluent, popular and easy to understand. For example:

paragraphs.source_en: In the poet's time, writers were much influenced by the “nyen-ngag” poetic style; the fashion of esteeming elegance and profundity and pursuing ornate verbal piling-up prevailed. Yet the poet Tsangyang Gyatso insisted on writing colloquial language into his poems, making Songs of Love lively and vivid in language, fresh, bright, joyful, popular, and easy to understand. It stood apart in its own style, refreshed the literary world of the time, held a distinctive place in Tibetan poetry, and possessed artistic charm; for this reason it has circulated widely among the Tibetan people for more than two hundred years.

units.source_zh: 诗人所处的时代，文人多受“年阿”诗体的影响，崇尚典雅深奥、讲求词藻堆砌之风盛行，而诗人仓央嘉措却坚持将通俗语言写入诗篇，使《情歌》语言活泼生动，清新明快乐，通俗易懂，独树一帜，一新当时文坛耳目，在藏族诗歌中别具一格，富有艺术魅力，所以二百多年来一直在藏族民间广泛流传。

paragraphs.source_en: Tsangyang Gyatso, the Sixth Dalai Lama, was a god-king, a saint of love, and a poet. He stayed in the human world, though only for a brief twenty-five years. His brief stay among humankind seems to have been for the very purpose of leaving behind these poems. paragraphs.source_en: Maji Ami literally means “unmarried young woman” or “unwed maiden”; it is said that the yellow house on Barkhor Street is the very home of the young woman in the poem, or, according to another version, the place where Tsangyang Gyatso, traveling incognito under the youthful name Dangsang Wangpo, met his lover in secret. This small yellow building stands proudly and has become a kind of symbol, while Tsangyang Gyatso's poems have always been widely recited and sung in Tibet. In the poems there is the shyness of a first encounter, the joy of mutual affection, the regret of missing one another by a hair, the steadfastness of vows as firm as mountains and seas, and also resentment toward a faithless turning away. Because of the author's particular identity, all love ultimately points toward disillusionment; thus the god-king experienced more deeply than ordinary people the sufferings of life in meeting what one hates and parting from what one loves, and the helplessness of seeking what cannot be obtained and longing for what cannot be fulfilled. Yet the more this is so, the more it throws into relief the preciousness and beauty of human love.

paragraphs.source_zh: 玛吉阿米直译为“未嫁少女”、“未嫁娘”；据说八廓街的黄房子正是诗中这位少女居家之地，或说是微服出行的仓央嘉措以少年宕桑汪波的名义与情人幽会之处。这幢黄颜色的小楼骄傲地存在并成为某种象征，仓央嘉措的诗歌在西藏一直被广为传颂。诗中有初识乍遇的羞怯，有两情相悦的欢欣，有失之交臂的惋惜，有山盟海誓的坚贞，也有对于负心背离的怨尤。由于作者特定的身份，所有的爱情最终指向的是幻灭，所以神王比常人更多地体验到怨憎会、爱别离的人生苦难和求不得、恨不能的无奈。然而愈是如此，便愈加凸显示出人间情爱的珍贵美好。

paragraphs.source_en: Today, Tsangyang Gyatso's life and fate are already widely known; his love poems have been translated into more than twenty languages and spread throughout the world, and new translations continue to appear even now. In Chinese translation alone over the past century, I have seen no fewer than seven or eight versions: some in folk-song style, some in five-character or seven-character verse, and some in modern free verse. Through their derivative influence, these poems likewise provide inexhaustible inspiration and creative resources for contemporary painters and musicians. In particular, the love songs of Tsangyang Gyatso, lovingly fashioned by outstanding contemporary composers and singers, possess an exceptional charm; human love, encouraged and blessed by Tsangyang Gyatso, gains an added divine radiance.

paragraphs.source_zh: 如今仓央嘉措的身世遭际已经广为人知，他的情诗被译成20多种文字传遍了全世界，至今仍不乏新的译作出现。仅仅是近百年间的汉语翻译，我所见到的就不下七八个版本：有民歌体的，有五言、七言体的，有现代新诗的。由派生而影响，这些诗作同样给当代画家、音乐家提供着不竭的灵感和创作资源。特别是经由当代优秀作曲家和歌手倾情打造的仓氏情歌格外的具有魅力，经由仓央嘉措鼓励和加持的人间情爱平添了神性光彩。
